title: Dynamic soft-band preemption with spillback-to-host and cache-reservation for SLO-aware continuous batching
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Problem: Continuous batching improves throughput but causes long-tail latency spikes when GPU memory becomes contended and KV working sets grow. Existing hard preemption rules evict cold KV entries aggressively or bluntly tear down slices; this harms tail SLOs for tenants with hot prefixes and increases re-warm cost. We need a preemption and fairness policy that preserves tenant tail latency SLOs while reclaiming GPU memory for higher-priority slices and maintaining overall throughput.

Goal: Implement a dynamic, SLO-aware preemption policy ('soft-band preemptor') that: 1) exposes per-tenant soft time-bands borrowers can use for burst windows, 2) selectively spills lower-impact KV shards to host memory (spillback) with async prefetch, 3) accounts for KV warm-up cost when deciding eviction order, and 4) enforces long-term fairness via a lightweight debt/credit ledger. The policy should be pluggable into the existing slice allocator and batch preemptor, instrumented for rollback and A/B testing, and ship behind runtime-1.20 feature flag.
technical_design:
Overview: Introduce two cooperating components: (a) SoftBandManager and DebtLedger; (b) SpillbackAgent.

SoftBandManager: tenants are assigned a nominal SLO weight and a soft-band token budget (time or memory tokens). At runtime tenants may borrow tokens beyond nominal allocation for a configurable grace window (soft-band). Borrowing creates debt entries in DebtLedger. Debt is repaid by future throttling or by denying future soft-band requests. Preemption is applied in two modes: soft reclaim (yield, slow drain, preserve hot KV) and hard reclaim (evict slices/terminate) only when debt>threshold or safety budget exceeded.

Eviction scoring: combine metrics into a single score: eviction_score = alpha * coldness + beta * host-residency-cost + gamma * slo_risk + delta * predicted_rewarm_tokens. Coldness estimated from LRU-ish access histograms per shard and model prefix. Host-residency-cost estimates async prefetch latency derived from measured host->GPU PCIe/DP bandwidth. SLO risk uses tenant-specific tail latency percentile and active request deadlines.

SpillbackAgent: On score favoring spillback, select KV shards to compress and copy to host pinned allocator. Metadata kept in lightweight page table; on a miss, asynchronous prefetch is enqueued and the request proceeds with an optimistic small-batch fallback (shorter model or cheaper variant). Spillback is prioritized for shards with high rewarm cost and low immediate hotness. A background reconstructor opportunistically rehydrates hot shards when predicted next-access probability crosses threshold.

Fairness ledger: DebtLedger is periodically decayed and exposed to observability. If a tenant accumulates unreasonable debt, automatic backpressure is applied at ingress (rate limiter) or by moving low-priority work to dedicated capacity.

Integration points: slice allocator (preempt decision), KV manager (spill/rehydrate APIs), runtime scheduler (soft vs hard reclaim hooks), console metrics (debt, spillback rate, rewarm latency). Feature-flagged and gated behind runtime-1.20 config toggles.
acceptance_criteria: SoftBandManager and SpillbackAgent implemented and feature-flaggable under runtime-1.20
Unit and integration tests covering soft reclaim, hard reclaim escalation, and spillback failure modes
Benchmarks: for synthetic mixed tenant workload, P95 tail latency improves by >=20% compared to baseline hard-evict policy while throughput loss <=5%
DebtLedger metrics surfaced in Console: per-tenant debt, recent borrow events, spillback bytes, rewarm latency histogram
Canary rollout plan documented and automated rollback in case debt-based starvation observed
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (dev): API/agent unit tests + local simulation (dev rigs) - feature flag off by default
Stage 2 (canary): enable soft-band+spillback for 5% of runtime nodes with synthetic workload; measure P50/P95/P99 and spillback rehits
Stage 3 (gradual): expand to 25% then 50% nodes over 2 weeks, monitor debt growth and customer SLO alerts
Stage 4 (release): enable by default with opt-out per-tenant; ship observability dashboards and docs
Rollback: immediate feature flag off and automatic migration to preexisting eviction policy if rewarm latencies or debt exceed thresholds
test_plan: unit tests for eviction_score calculations with synthetic histograms
integration test: KV miss -> spillback -> async prefetch -> successful rewarm
stress test: concurrent borrowers + repeated rewarm to validate debt repayment logic
long-running sim (48h): mixed tenant workload replay from production traces to measure cumulative debt and throughput
chaos test: simulate PCIe slowdown and validate fallback to cheaper model variant
